heuristic.applicability: Prefer when target_pose is reliable and the drawer is open, particularly near cavity alignment, lowering, opening, release confirmation, retreat, and handle transition, or whenever the destination/drawer is displaced relative to training. It is also the preferred cover after an off-center but valid deposit because its retreat and handle targets do not shift with the settled block.

handoff.entry_conditions: Drawer open/stable; target_pose available; block plausibly held or already over the cavity; measured joints admit a collision-free approach in the demonstrated responsibility.
handoff.exit_conditions: Block rests inside the cavity at drawer-floor height and is detached; TCP retreats above the cavity and reaches the handle approach, ready for close_drawer.
handoff.failure_signatures: Target pose jumps or is unavailable, block does not follow closed TCP before release, descent is outside cavity bounds, object remains suspended after opening, or IK residual/limit diagnostics indicate the shifted fixture target is unreachable.
handoff.overlap_role: Retains every 680:1160 action. The 680:840 retrieval overlap covers the transfer into destination coordinates; the 900:1160 closing overlap covers release confirmation, retreat and fixture-relative handle approach/grasp.
handoff.successor_readiness: close_drawer may take over in the shared 900:1160 region, but must not move the drawer until object z is at floor height and two frames show it stationary relative to the drawer. Late handoff occurs with TCP near the handle and object deposited.

heuristic.limitations: The destination frame is assumed to move rigidly with the relevant drawer geometry and to be accurately observed. A large held-block displacement is not removed from the input/action mapping by construction, and the model may choose a memorized approach before it has re-aligned the object. Relative decoding does not ensure cavity clearance, attachment, or IK feasibility. Demonstrations contain no recovery from a premature drop.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: The high-level agent may enter from retrieval or from the object-frame prior before/over the cavity. It should keep this prior through release and post-release retreat when the destination is displaced. If the held object begins far from demonstrated destination-relative entry support, use the object-frame policy for the transfer; if current release phase is ambiguous or the TCP is locally perturbed, use the phase-aware local policy. close_drawer receives through 900:1160 only after settling.
heuristic.rationale: Observed: transport converges above target_pose near x=-0.175,y=0 before descent (demo12100 indices 840-900); after opening, the object settles near z=0.063 while TCP holds near z=0.126 (920), rises (940-960), then moves to the handle approach near x=-0.44 (1080-1159). target_pose tracks the drawer coordinate through its world x value. Likely deployment failure: displacement of the drawer or target makes memorized world coordinates miss the cavity or handle corridor. Mechanism: destination-canonical history and destination-relative labels/decoding make all Cartesian targets rigidly follow the observed destination frame while measured qpos/qvel retain reachability/posture information. Expected benefit is destination displacement equivariance, not evidence of unseen-displacement success.
heuristic.statement: Live destination-frame cavity anchoring: diffuse commanded TCP pose as translation (m), canonical unit quaternion wxyz, and gripper scalar relative to the current target_pose. Decode through the freshly observed destination frame at every slot. This targets displacement of the open drawer/placement goal and keeps lowering, release, retreat, and the fixture-relative transition toward the handle anchored to the drawer rather than to where the block happens to settle.

subgoal: Carry the extracted block from above the tunnel to the open drawer, align it over the cavity, descend, open the gripper to leave the block resting at drawer-floor height, then retreat without disturbing it and reorient toward the drawer handle. Contact is maintained with the block until release. Approximate entry: block held high outside the tunnel, drawer open. Approximate exit: block resting in the open drawer near z=0.063 and x about -0.166 to -0.177 in the open-drawer world pose, gripper free and at/near the handle approach.
